system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: Two network logon attempts for raj.iyer failed with an incorrect-password status, using NTLM, from 198.51.100.77 at 13:40:13 and 13:41:28 UTC.
At 13:42:52 UTC, the domain controller recorded a successful network logon for raj.iyer using Kerberos, with the same source IP address, 198.51.100.77.

The successful logon from 198.51.100.77 is inconsistent with the supplied environment context: there is no VPN, and remote administration is only performed from WS-KORTEGA-01 inside the office. This makes the successful authentication concerning, though the record alone does not establish who initiated it.

Earlier in the window, raj.iyer had a successful interactive logon on WS-RIYER-01 and Kerberos activity associated with internal address 10.20.10.23; this differs from the later authentication recorded from 198.51.100.77.

known_telemetry_limitations: The successful authentication record identifies the source IP and a workstation name of DC-LV-01, but the available records do not independently validate the source or explain that attribution; treat the source identity as unconfirmed (S01-00048).
The supplied records show authentication events but do not provide the initiating client process or subsequent activity tied to the successful logon session (S01-00048).
The records establish that a successful logon followed the failures, but do not establish that the successful logon was caused by the same actor or attempt.
claims_not_established: The identity or location of the person or system that initiated the failed and successful logons (S01-00046, S01-00047, S01-00048).
Whether raj.iyer’s credentials were compromised or the successful logon was authorized (S01-00048).
Whether the successful session accessed resources or performed further actions on the domain controller (S01-00048).
additional_evidence_needed: Correlate DC-LV-01 authentication and Kerberos ticket logs around 13:40–13:43 UTC, including any related 4768, 4769, and logon-session events.
Validate the source address and its network attribution using firewall, router, DHCP, and other available network records.
Review domain-controller and account activity after the successful logon, and confirm with raj.iyer and IT whether the authentication was expected.
